hypothesis: Combining early exit acceleration (threshold 2.0) with mixed continuation disabling to maximize pass count and reduce Monte Carlo variance.
rationale: Experiment 9 showed disabling mixed continuation was near-neutral (+0.0003) but saves compute time by not running the greedy fallback. By pairing this efficiency gain with a lower early-exit t-stat threshold (2.0 instead of 2.5), we can dramatically increase the number of evaluation passes within the 300s budget. This combination strategy aims to reduce overall variance without hurting decision quality on marginal spots.
